title: HW1: Sorting Algorithms
description: Write a program that reads whitespace-separated integers from standard input and prints them in ascending order on one line, separated by single spaces. Submit the program and a short report explaining the approach. For example, "3 1 2" prints "1 2 3", "3 1 2 1 3" prints "1 1 2 3 3", "-3 1 -2 0 5" prints "-3 -2 0 1 5" and "42" prints "42".

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Produces correctly sorted output for any valid input, including duplicates, negative numbers, a single value, and input that is already sorted or reversed.

criteria.name: Input and Output
criteria.description: Reads the integers from standard input and prints them on one line separated by single spaces, with no extra text.

criteria.name: Code Quality
criteria.description: The code is readable and appropriate for an introductory course.

criteria.name: Report: Approach
criteria.description: The report explains the approach clearly and why it produces sorted output.

criteria.name: Report: Analysis
criteria.description: The report gives a correct time complexity and discusses edge cases.

guidance: Be encouraging but rigorous. Using the built-in sort is expected and should not be penalized. Focus feedback on algorithmic understanding, not code style. This is an introductory assignment, so set expectations accordingly.
